org.agentvibe.seeds.$comment: DERIVED, not authored. DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md gives three faces and 'running text near 65 characters' and NO NUMBERS AT ALL, so the ramp below is a derivation and is stated as one. UI BAND: base 12, +2, five steps -> 12 14 16 18 20. That is vercel.com's measured marketing increment (+2, over 12 14 16) extended two steps, and every one of the five sizes appears in stripe.com's measured band; the range 12-20 is exactly the span 7.1 states for the UI band. It is deliberately NOT agentvibe's 11-15 control-plane band: 18 is the reading size for long-form prose, with 16 below it for dense passages and 20 above it for a lead. DISPLAY BAND: base 32, +16, three steps -> 32 48 64. +16 is the modal display increment in the corpus (linear.app +16 +16, stripe.com +16) and all three sizes are directly measured there (stripe.com 32 and 48, linear.app 48 and 64, vercel.com 64). THE JOIN is 20 -> 32, a ratio of 1.6 against a widest in-band step of 1.167 — a jump, not an interpolation. LEADING: peak 1.56 at 18px puts the top of 7.1's sourced 1.5-1.56 band exactly on the reading size, which is the right end of that band for a marketing site rather than a control plane. falloff 0.45 with exponent 1.0 gives 1.41 1.46 1.51 1.56 1.51 across the UI band; the exponent is 1 because nothing in the corpus argues for a curve shape and the linear falloff is the fit with one fewer invented constant. TRACKING: zeroAt 14 is 7.1's crossover. slope 0.0006 is set from the LARGE end, not the small one — this band spans 12 to 64px, 5.3x, and one linear function cannot give both a visible positive value at 12px and a sane negative one at 64px. 0.0006 yields -0.03em at the 64px hero and -0.02em at 48px, which is conventional for a high-contrast display serif; the consequence is that the positive tracking at 12px is +0.0012em, real in sign and invisible in effect. The uppercase-label letter-spacing DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md calls for is NOT this token: it is bound to case, not to size, and no size-derived function can express it.

family.$comment: TWO SLOTS, THREE FACES — the one thing in DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md's type section that this schema cannot hold. Instrument Serif (display: regular and italic only, no bold, so display emphasis is size and italic and never weight) has no slot: buildModel reads family.sans and family.mono and nothing else, so a serif key would reach no stylesheet and no TypeScript export. It is left out deliberately. CONSEQUENCE TO CARRY FORWARD: the display band below (32 48 64) is where Instrument Serif belongs, and under these tokens alone it would inherit --font-sans. The display face has to be bound at the component layer until the generator grows a third slot.
family.sans: 'Schibsted Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
family.mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace
